column1: # Measure gates for cpl_ibm3 (execution-manifest contract: !measures).
# Why measures: a single TXL and two CPL bundles (2- and 4-conductor) fed
# through L-C ladders and clamped by diodes, stepped at the 0.2 ns deck
# step against a 1.1 ns edge. Every gated quantity is a reflected or
# coupled wavefront, and the reference is not converged on its own grid:
# refining ngspice-46's step 10x moves its crossings by up to 17 ps
# (v(8) fall) and its peaks by up to 3.8 percent (v(3)), so pointwise
# agreement at the deck step would measure grid reproduction. RSpice's
# free run lands inside that refinement movement on most quantities and
# on the same side of the reference as its refined answer.
# History: this deck was the one free-running collapse in the corpus.
# Its inductors kept the transient on the node-voltage LTE estimator,
# whose predictor error at the 0 V far-end nodes hit by the first CPL
# wave (t ~ 0.8 ns, ~4.5 GV/s) demanded ~1e-16 s steps and spiralled to
# 1e-19 s. ngspice steps this deck on charge and flux truncation alone
# (CAPtrunc/INDtrunc); with the flux walk in place RSpice does the same.
# Source: VES PULSE 0->5 V, 1.1 ns rise at t=0. v(6)/v(7)/v(8) sit at the
# driven end and first CPL, v(3) after the first CPL's ladder, v(11) after
# the TXL, v(15) at the far end of the 4-conductor CPL. Tolerances are
# twice the larger of the reference's 10x-refinement movement and RSpice's
# deviation (the larger of its trapezoidal and TrapGear runs).
